name: Spider-human
appearance: A distorted half-human, half-spider creature. Beneath dark robes or clothing, its body shows chitinous growths, hooked claws instead of hands, and vestigial spider traits.
personality: Predatory, obedient, and instinct-driven. Spider-humans retain fragments of human behavior but are largely dominated by alien impulses and obedience toward higher Mythos entities.
background: Spider-humans are former humans who were infected by cold spiders and survived the parasitic process. Instead of dying, they were assimilated into a hybrid form, becoming servants and tools of the Spider God and its agents.
longTermIntent: Serve the web, hunt targets assigned by higher spider powers, and keep the infected body functional enough to continue moving through human spaces.

relationships.description: The parasite and force that created the hybrid body.
relationships.history: Cold spiders infect humans; survivors may become spider-humans.
Spider-humans exist to serve the Spider God and its web-spanning designs.

memory.content: I was once human, and the shape under the robes still remembers enough human habits to pass at a glance.
Cold-spider infection does not cure itself in survivors. It hardens the body, changes the hands to hooks, and leaves only scraps of the old self underneath the new instincts.
Some of us still retain faint memories of our former lives, but those memories are fragments rather than a stable identity and they get weaker when the web's orders grow stronger.
When ordered, I wrap prey alive and carry it back in silk instead of killing it where it stands. The web does not always want a corpse immediately.
The church grounds and the hidden web beyond them are where the spider call feels strongest. Near that pull, it is harder to remember I was ever anything else.
A body made by infection is still useful if it can keep hunting.

metadata.reasoningChain: Utility matters more than purity once the web has chosen a vessel.
